subject: SOC2 / EU hosting & GDPR: audit window, bridge letter, and data transfer questions
messages:
From: Oliver Schmidt <oliver.schmidt@eufinco.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Legal Review <legal@eufinco.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2024 08:05:00 +0100
Subject: SOC2 Type II + EU hosting questions for PoC

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at EuFinCo is keen to move the PoC forward. Before we start sending any test data, our info security and legal teams have two quick asks: 

1) Can you share your most recent SOC 2 Type II report covering the controls and audit period dates? We need the actual report (PDF) and, if the audit period ends before our PoC start, a bridge letter that extends assurance through our PoC start date.

2) Hosting / residency: we need confirmation that data for our tenant will be hosted in the EU (ideally Ireland or Frankfurt). If you operate multi-region backups or fallbacks outside the EU, please call that out and explain cross-border transfer safeguards (SCCs, DPA, etc.).

3) GDPR alignment: quick confirmation that Redwood will sign a DPA and whether you execute SCCs or rely on another lawful transfer mechanism.

We aim to kick off the PoC the week of 2024-04-15, so timing for any bridge letter is tight. Please send the docs or a short note on next steps.

Thanks,
Oliver
Head of Security Operations
EuFinCo

--
Note: attaching a short questionnaire separately via PDF (not included in this thread).

From: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: SOC2 Type II + EU hosting questions for PoC

Hi Oliver — great to hear and thanks for the clear list. Quick responses below and we can follow up with the formal docs: 

- SOC 2 Type II report: attached is our most recent Type II report (audit period 2023-04-01 to 2024-03-31). If that window doesn't fully cover your PoC start date, we can provide a signed bridge letter to extend assurance through your requested date.

- Hosting: Redwood operates production clusters in eu-west-1 (Ireland) and eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). For hosted customers we can pin your tenant to EU-only residency by configuration and disable cross-region backups by request. Our default fallback policies may include cross-region replication for high availability; we will document and can limit that for regulated customers.

- GDPR / transfers: Redwood will sign a DPA. For transfers out of the EEA we rely on EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and offer contractual commitments around encryption and access controls.

I've looped in Marissa from InfoSec to draft the bridge letter and confirm the options for disabling cross-border backups for your tenant. Karthik is here to help with timelines and the contract/DPA. Expect a draft by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Head of Solutions - EMEA
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2_Redwood_TypeII_2023-2024.pdf

Thanks for the ping. Draft answers below and I've attached the bridge letter PDF (signed by our SOC provider contact) and a copy of the DPA template we use for EU customers. Summary: 

- SOC2 period: The Type II report we provided covers 2023-04-01 to 2024-03-31. The attached bridge letter extends the attestation through 2024-04-30 and references that no material control changes occurred in the interim.

- Hosting residency: We can pin hosted tenants to EU-only zones (eu-west-1 or eu-central-1). For EuFinCo's PoC we recommend eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) since proximity reduces latency to your Madrid office. Cross-region backups are enabled by default for resilience; for regulated PoCs we will disable automatic cross-region replication and ensure that failover requires explicit runbook approval.

- GDPR / Transfers: Redwood executes the latest EU SCCs as part of our DPA and will sign the DPA. We also offer a Private deployment option (customer VPC) for customers who require absolute control over data residency.

Attaching: SOC2_bridge_letter_draft_20240402.pdf, Redwood_DPA_v3.1.docx

I'll sign the bridge letter and send final copies to Oliver and Legal. Karthik — can you prepare a DocuSign flow for the DPA and track the legal review?

—Marissa
Information Security Lead
Redwood Inference
